column1: National Conference of the American Association for Artificial Intelligence
column12: A single AI review will be included in Phase 1, but will not include any scores or recommendations.
column13: AAAI 2026 runs a venue operated AI review system using a large frontier reasoning model from OpenAI to produce one supplementary AI review per paper in Phase 1, plus an AI summary in Phase 2. No human reviewer is replaced. The previous quote attributed to this FAQ was not present on the page when reverified on 13 May 2026; replaced with verbatim wording from question 7 of the FAQ.

column1: International Joint Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (previously the International Conference on Multiagent Systems, ICMAS, changed in 2000)

column1: Association for Computational Linguistics
column12: it is reasonable to use writing assistance to paraphrase the review, e.g. to help reviewers who are not native speakers of English
column13: ACL uses ARR for peer review. ARR policy permits LLMs for paraphrasing review text and for proof checking but bars generative assistance for creating the first draft of a review and bars uploading manuscripts or peer review reports to non privacy preserving generative tools. The previous quote was a paraphrase synthesis that did not appear verbatim on the page when reverified on 13 May 2026; replaced with verbatim wording.

column1: ACM Multimedia
column12: Reviewers may use generative AI or other third-party tools with the sole purpose of improving the quality and readability of reviewer reports for the author, provided any and all parts of the review that would potentially identify the submission, author identities, reviewer identity, or other confidential content is removed prior to uploading into third party tools.
column13: ACMMM 2025 reviewer and area chair guidelines page contains no reviewer LLM clause when reverified on 13 May 2026. ACMMM is ACM sponsored and inherits the ACM Peer Review Policy. Source URL updated from the ACMMM reviewer guidelines page to the ACM Peer Review Policy. The ACM policy permits readability polishing with confidentiality protected text removed.

column1: Conference on Learning Theory

column1: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
column12: Large language models (LLMs) are NOT allowed to be used for writing the reviews nor the meta-reviews at any step.
column13: CVPR 2025: LLMs may not be used to write reviews or meta reviews at any step. Narrow exceptions: background research, short phrase clarity checks, and grammar checker tools. Highly irresponsible review violations lead to desk rejection of the reviewer's own submissions.

column1: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation
column12: Reviewers are allowed to use AI tools to assist in reviewing (for example to improve their own writing, to ask for summaries of related works, etc.) only if they refrain from including any confidential content, which includes any content in submission itself.
column13: ACM EC 2026 follows ACM peer review policy. Reviewer AI tool use permitted for own writing improvement and related work summaries with confidentiality preserved. Note: EC 2026 also runs an optional author side experimental program Refine.ink offering pre submission feedback via an LLM based service.
